newsitem.title: USA: Quaker sharehodler pushes beverage spinoff.
newsitem.headline: Quaker sharehodler pushes beverage spinoff.

text.p: A Quaker Oats Co shareholder will propose the company separate its food business from its beverage business, which includes the embattled Snapple line, according to the proxy statement filed in advance of the company's annual meeting.
The proposal, to be introduced by Leland Chalmers, a holder of 50,732 common shares, calls for Quaker to split the two businesses into two sepearate companies by no later than December 31.
A proposal by Chalmers last year that the company retain an investment banking firm to analyze this issue received only 11 percent of shares voting, the proxy said.,
Quaker Oats' board recommended unanimously against the separation proposal.

"The board believes that it can function most effectively when its strategic planning is conducted confidentially," the proxy said. "In this way, ideas can be developed and debated without the fear that they will lead to rumors or public debate that could harmfully restrict the board's choices or disrupt the public market for the company's stock. Therefore, the board believes that adoption of the proposal could actually diminish shareholder value."
The Snapple business has been under fire as it has posted an operating loss since it was acquired two years ago in a $1.8 billion transaction.
Quaker Oats will hold its annual meeting May 14 in Rosemont, Illinois.
